request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to the sheet now writes a line to the audit file, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**What I changed:** the four endpoints that change a sheet (add person, edit person, add claim, edit claim) each get one new step that writes the line. It runs right after the save step, inside the same transaction, and before the response is sent. Each step is its own small class:
- `person/AuditPersonAdded` writes `PERSON_ADDED sheet=… by=… name=… grade=…`
- `person/AuditPersonEdited` writes `PERSON_EDITED …` with the same fields
- `claim/AuditClaimAdded` writes `CLAIM_ADDED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=…`
- `claim/AuditClaimEdited` writes `CLAIM_EDITED …` with the same fields

The signed-in user already comes in with every request, so the front end didn't need to change. Amounts and dates are formatted by the same code that formats them for the screen (`ClaimResponse.from`), so the file always matches what the screen shows: `6.00`, `2026-03-02`. When a claim has no date, the line records the date that was actually saved, which is the sheet's "today". I also added "not even an audit line" to the comment at the top of each endpoint's YAML.

**Refused changes write nothing.** Every refusal rule, current and future, runs as a step before the save, so a refusal stops the request before it reaches the audit step. A name already in use is caught by its own check before the save.

**One limitation:** the audit line is written before the database commit, and a file write can't be undone. If the commit failed after the line was written (e.g. the database failed at that moment), the file would show a change that never landed. Nothing in the current flow triggers this. Moving the audit step after the commit would close the gap, but it would also make it harder to guarantee the lines stay in the same order as the changes.
